Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposal: Reserve Guardrails + Burst Toggle for Acme.ai evaluation -> commit

Hi Jamie / Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really appreciate the clarity around your evaluation success criteria (latency p95 < 300ms, inference cost target <$0.004/token, and 3-week pilot ingesting 10k daily requests). Per our agreement, attached is a short MAP + reservation proposal that ties commercial milestones to the evaluation gates so we can move quickly to a committed Dedicated pool if the pilot hits signals.

High-level summary (see attachments for numbers):
- Pilot: 2-week controlled evaluation on a 16-GPU pool (A100-equivalent), auto-scaling to 24 GPUs for peak tests.
- MAP milestones: Week 1 perf baseline; Week 2 quality/regression pass; decision gate at Day 14.
- Commitment options: 12m or 24m term. 12m = 8% discount vs on-demand; 24m = 15% discount + 1-month free in-year 1.
- Burst toggle / guardrails: Burst allowed up to 2x baseline for up to 72 hours/month at no extra charge (consumes burst credits). Overage above burst = 1.5x unit rate. Bursts beyond monthly credits require advance notice or temporary capacity increase.
- Ramp schedule: initial reserved baseline = 16 GPUs, ramp to 32 GPUs by month 3 for the 24m plan (stair-step milestones).

Open items where we'd love Acme confirmation: exact baseline GPU size for your steady-state (we proposed 16), preferred term (12 vs 24), and whether procurement needs changes to the burst allowance language.

I looped Ben (pricing) and Monica (CS/ops) to confirm the operational and billing mechanics. If this looks good, I can convert the MAP to a signature-ready DocuSign and we can start the pilot next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Proposal: Reserve Guardrails + Burst Toggle for Acme.ai evaluation -> commit

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side after reviewing with infra and procurement: 

1) Baseline sizing: 16 GPUs sounds reasonable as a starting point. Our internal load tests show steady-state closer to 12, but we want buffer for launches. Can we set baseline to 12 with an agreed ramp to 24 on milestone M2?
2) Burst: the 2x/72-hour allowance is helpful. Procurement is asking for a defined pool of "burst credits" per quarter rather than implicit hours. Can you propose credits and how they convert to GPU-hours?
3) Term: leaning towards 24m if the financials have the ramp built in. We need an explicit SLA credit for availability <99.5%.
4) Pricing: can Ben share a simple table showing effective $/GPU-hour under each term and discount, including overage pricing?

If you can update the MAP with those specific numbers and a short example of a burst-credit conversion, we can get procurement to review next week.

—Jamie
VP Engineering, Acme.ai

Jamie / Vanessa —

Quick pricing table below (exported also to resv_pricing_table.xlsx). Numbers are illustrative but match our commercial deck assumptions. I'll put the detailed line items into the MAP doc and convert the burst allowance into quarterly credits.

Baseline assumptions: A100-equivalent GPU cost (list-rate) = $X (proprietary internal price used for parity)

Option A — 12m term
- Baseline reserved: 12 GPUs
- Commitment discount: 8% off list
- Effective $/GPU-hour: $0.85 (example)
- Burst guardrail: 2x for up to 36 GPU-hours per week (quarterly cap = 468 GPU-hours). Overage = 1.5x effective rate.

Option B — 24m term
- Baseline reserved: 12 GPUs with scheduled ramp to 24 GPUs at month 3
- Commitment discount: 15% off list + 1-month free in year 1
- Effective $/GPU-hour: $0.72 (example)
- Burst guardrail: 2x for up to 60 GPU-hours per week (quarterly cap = 780 GPU-hours). Overage = 1.25x effective rate (more favorable).

Notes on burst credits conversion: 1 GPU-hour credit = 1 GPU operating for 1 hour. We propose quarterly buckets so accounting is predictable; unused credits do not roll forward but can be rebalanced during enterprise review windows.

SLA: For availability below 99.5% measured at the model endpoint level, we provide service credits = 5% of monthly reserved fee for every 0.1% below the threshold, capped at 50%. We will add an exclusion for force majeure and scheduled maintenance.

If that aligns, Vanessa — can you confirm Acme wants baseline set at 12 GPUs (Ben's table uses that) and whether procurement wants the quarterly credit numbers in the main SOW or Annex A?

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Team —

This is very helpful. Procurement reviewed Ben's table and we can proceed with the following for the signature-ready MAP:

- Baseline reserved: 12 GPUs, ramp to 24 at month 3 (24m term).
- Burst credits: quarterly bucket = 780 GPU-hours (as in Option B). Procurement requests the quarterly bucket called out in Annex B with examples.
- Overage rate: 1.25x effective rate for over-burst usage.
- SLA: 99.5% availability target, with the credit formula Ben specified. Please add a clause for a 30-day cure period prior to credits applying so we have a remediation window.
- DocuSign: procurement needs a downloadable SOW + Annexes. Please send by EOD Monday.

If Redwood can include a simple monthly illustration of expected $/month based on the ramp (for finance), we'll fast-track signature.
